arxiv-2102-09083.title: Two-dimensional easy-plane SU ( 3 ) (3) magnet with the transverse field: Anisotropy-driven multicriticality
arxiv-2102-09083.creator: Yoshihiro Nishiyama
arxiv-2102-09083.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yoshihiro Nishiyama. The two-dimensional easy-plane SU ( 3 ) (3) magnet subjected to the transverse field was investigated with the exact-diagonalization method. So far, as to the X ​ Y XY model (namely, the easy-plane SU ( 2 ) (2) magnet), the transverse-field-driven order-disorder phase boundary has been investigated with the exact-diagonalization method, and it was claimed that the end-point singularity (multicriticality) at the X ​ X XX -symmetric point does not accord with large- N N -theory’s prediction.

arxiv-2303-16949.title: Concise QBF Encodings for Games on a Grid (extended version)
arxiv-2303-16949.creator: Irfansha Shaik, Jaco van de Pol
arxiv-2303-16949.description: Abstract Encoding 2-player games in QBF correctly and efficiently is challenging and error-prone. To enable concise specifications and uniform encodings of games played on grid boards, like Tic-Tac-Toe, Connect-4, Domineering, Pursuer-Evader and Breakthrough, we introduce BDDL – Board-game Domain Definition Language , inspired by the success of PDDL in the planning domain.

arxiv-2402-19083.title: AB Dor: Coronal imaging and activity cycles
arxiv-2402-19083.creator: Gurpreet Singh, J. C. Pandey
arxiv-2402-19083.description: Abstract Using long-term X-ray observations, we present the short-term and long-term X-ray variability analysis of the ultra-fast rotating active star AB Dor. Flaring events are common in X-ray observations of AB Dor and occupy a substantial portion of the total observation time, averaging around 57 ± \pm 23%.

arxiv-2404-07068.title: Entanglement entropy in the ground state of non-interacting massless Dirac fermions in dimension one
arxiv-2404-07068.creator: Fabrizio Ferro, Paul Pfeiffer and Wolfgang Spitzer
arxiv-2404-07068.description: Abstract . We present a novel proof of a formula of Casini and Huerta for the entanglement entropy of the ground state of non-interacting massless Dirac fermions in dimension one localized to (a union of) intervals and generalize it to the case of Rényi entropies. At first, we prove that these entropies are well-defined for non-intersecting intervals.

arxiv-2407-06626.title: Kuroda’s Translation for the λ ​ Π \lambda\Pi -Calculus Modulo Theory and Dedukti
arxiv-2407-06626.creator: Thomas Traversié
arxiv-2407-06626.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas Traversié. Kuroda’s translation embeds classical first-order logic into intuitionistic logic, through the insertion of double negations. Recently, Brown and Rizkallah extended this translation to higher-order logic. In this paper, we adapt it for theories encoded in higher-order logic in the λ ​ Π \lambda\Pi -calculus modulo theory, a logical framework that extends λ \lambda -calculus with dependent types and user-defined rewrite rules.

arxiv-2410-22255.title: Optimizing Cost through Dynamic Stochastic Resetting
arxiv-2410-22255.creator: Deepak Gupta, Bart Cleuren
arxiv-2410-22255.description: Abstract The cost of stochastic resetting is considered within the context of a discrete random walk model. In addition to standard stochastic resetting, for which a reset occurs with a certain probability after each step, we introduce a novel resetting protocol which we dubbed dynamic resetting .

arxiv-2602-03121.title: Behind the Feed: A Taxonomy of User-Facing Cues for Algorithmic Transparency in Social Media
arxiv-2602-03121.creator: Haoze Guo, Ziqi Wei
arxiv-2602-03121.description: Abstract People who use social media are learning about how the companies that run these platforms make their decisions on who gets to see what through visual indicators in the interface (UI) of each social media site. These indicators are different for each platform and are not always located in an easy-to-find location on the site.

pmc-10656622.title: Use of AgomiR and AntagomiR technologies to alter satellite cell proliferation in vitro, miRNA expression, and muscle fiber hypertrophy in intrauterine growth-restricted lambs
pmc-10656622.creator: M. A. Greene, G. A. Worley, A. N. S. Udoka, R. R. Powell, T. Bruce, J. L. Klotz, W. C. Bridges, S. K. Duckett
pmc-10656622.description: Introduction: microRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that work at the posttranscriptional level to repress gene expression. Several miRNAs are preferentially expressed in skeletal muscle and participate in myogenesis. This research was conducted to alter endogenous miRNA expression in skeletal muscle to promote muscle hypertrophy.

pmc-10668829.title: Emergence of Antibiotic-Resistant Porphyromonas gingivalis in United States Periodontitis Patients
pmc-10668829.creator: Thomas E. Rams, Jacqueline D. Sautter, Arie J. van Winkelhoff
pmc-10668829.description: Antibiotic resistance patterns of the major human periodontal pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis were assessed over a 20-year period in the United States. Subgingival P. gingivalis was cultured pre-treatment from 2193 severe periodontitis patients during three time periods: 1999–2000 (936 patients), 2009–2010 (685 patients), and 2019–2020 (572 patients).

pmc-11438243.title: Associations of sugar-sweetened beverage consumption and screen time with physical fitness index: a multicentre cross-sectional study among Chinese adolescents
pmc-11438243.creator: Zhanjiang Fan, Tao Shi, Yaorong Yang, Wenbin He, Di Chai
pmc-11438243.description: BackgroundPast research has focused on the analysis of the association between sugar-sweetened beverages consumption and screen time, respectively, and an indicator of physical fitness in adolescents. However, no studies have analyzed the interaction between sugar-sweetened beverage consumption and screen time on physical fitness index.

pmc-12481701.title: Identifying impacts of contact tracing on HIV epidemiological inference from phylogenetic data
pmc-12481701.creator: Michael D Kupperman, Ruian Ke, Thomas Leitner
pmc-12481701.description: Robust sampling methods are foundational to inferences using phylogenies. Yet the impact of using contact tracing, a type of non-uniform sampling used in public health applications such as infectious disease outbreak investigations, has not been investigated in the molecular epidemiology field.

pmc-12766839.title: Artificial intelligence-based assessment of central aortic haemodynamics using non-invasive pulse wave analysis in constrictive pericarditis
pmc-12766839.creator: Mathieu N Suleiman, Oliver Dewald, Helena Dreher, Ann-Sophie Kaemmerer-Suleiman, Frank Klawonn, Martin Middeke, Robert Pittrow, Frank Harig, Fritz Mellert
pmc-12766839.description: BackgroundConstrictive pericarditis (CP) is a rare but significant pericardial disease resulting in impaired ventricular filling and heart failure symptoms, often following cardiac surgery. Its clinical presentation complicates diagnosis, mimicking other causes of heart failure. Recent technological advances, including artificial intelligence (AI)-based non-invasive pulse wave analysis (AI-PWA), have the potential for improved haemodynamic assessment and clinical decision-making.

pmc-12838459.title: Non-suicidal self-injury links with multidimensional cognitive dysfunctions in adolescents with depression
pmc-12838459.creator: Shina Li, Xiuling Tian, Yihao Zhang, Ying Yang, Huijing Sun, Jiahui Chen, Defeng Xu, Feiyu Xu, Xingxing Zhu, Kangcheng Wang, Dongdong Qiao
pmc-12838459.description: BackgroundNon-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) has high prevalence among adolescents with mood disorders and is accompanied by cognitive impairments. Most existing studies have examined their impairments on single cognitive domains. It remains unclear which cognitive deficits are associated with adolescent NSSI and its functions and addictive features, from a multidimensional perspective.

pmc-13193340.title: Dietary cholesterol reduces blood pressure and alters lipid profiles in stroke-prone spontaneously hypertensive rats
pmc-13193340.creator: Yutaro Nishikata, Kenjiro Tatematsu, Yoshiaki Saito, Toshiyuki Matsunaga, Naoki Ohara, Luis Eduardo Quintas, Luis Eduardo Quintas, Luis Eduardo Quintas
pmc-13193340.description: Although cholesterol (Chol) is widely recognized as a risk factor for cardiovascular disease, dietary Chol intake has been reported to extend the lifespan of stroke-prone spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRSP). The mechanisms responsible for this paradoxical effect remain unclear. The present study examined changes in organ lipid profiles and associated molecular factors in SHRSP rats fed a Chol-enriched diet.

pmc-13194752.title: Correlation analysis between the collapsibility of loess and physicomechanical indices in Longdong region and prediction of the collapsibility coefficient based on machine learning
pmc-13194752.creator: Deren Liu, Kaiqiang Wang, Yicheng Bian, Xu Wang, Yanjie Zhang
pmc-13194752.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Against the backdrop of booming engineering construction in loess areas, achieving rapid and accurate prediction of the loess collapsibility coefficient is of great significance. This study takes the loess in the Longdong area as the research object. Based on analyzing the correlation between the collapsibility coefficient and various soil property indices, a rapid determination standard for the collapsibility of loess in this area is proposed.

pmc-13224112.title: Paediatric DNA methylation profile scores: a systematic review and open-source atlas
pmc-13224112.creator: Isabel K Schuurmans, Serena Defina, APC Hermans, Alexander Neumann, Matthew Suderman, Paul Yousefi, Janine F Felix, Charlotte AM Cecil
pmc-13224112.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryMethylation profile scores (MPSs) have emerged as a useful tool to index exposures, biological states, or disease-related patterns, by aggregating information across many DNA methylation (DNAm) sites into a single score per individual. Although most MPSs to date have been trained and validated in adults, their use in early life (<18 years) is rapidly gaining momentum, as more cohorts profile DNAm during development, offering a window on exposures and vulnerability before disease onset.

uslaw-usc-t31-s3724.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s3724.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 37 (Claims); Subchapter III (Claims Against The United States Government). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The Attorney General may settle, for not more than $50,000 in any one case, a claim for personal injury, death, or damage to, or loss of, privately owned property, caused by an investigative or law enforcement officer.
